lines.en: : So! Now that you guys have spent a good thirty minutes each on Sensei, do I get a turn as well? Or is this the part where we remember this is a group setting and that we should be together as a group?
: Hey, don’t look at me. I had a good reason. Maya was just impatient.
: Yes. That is me, alright. An impatient person who’s entirely incapable of ever waiting for anything.
: Great! Then I guess that means we’re finally ready for some sort of activity we can all do together.
: Under normal circumstances, I’d suggest karaoke on account of being inside a karaoke booth. But it seems that no one cares about that tonight, so I guess we’ll have to figure something else out!
: I like when you get all passive aggressive. It doesn’t happen very often. But when it does, it’s fun.
: Well, I’m glad you find it amusing! Now, does anyone have any suggestions?
: We could play truth or dare? We’ve never done it with Sensei before.
: That’s likely on account of what you’d all dare him to do.
: Bold of you to assume he’d choose “dare” instead of truth.
: Not when you remember he’s a novice at best when it comes to honesty and an incorrigible pervert with complete awareness that all of you would just dare him to kiss you.
: Why stop there when you can dare him to kill everyone in the room and live with you happily ever after?
: This. This is why we have not played truth or dare with Sensei.
: Yeah, and I’m starting to feel like we should keep things that way. There’s gotta be something, though.
: Do you have any ideas, Sana? You’ve been pretty quiet ever since I got back.
: Sana’s pretty quiet all the time. This shouldn’t come as a surprise to you, Ami.
: I...um...I don’t really...know many games...
: At least...not the kind you...play in person...
: Oh, come on! You’ve gotta know something! Let that extrovert you keep locked inside the closet loose, my girl! We’re the closest friends you’ve got!
: Um...there’s...uhh...the King’s Game?...
: Strip poker it is!
: We don’t even have any cards.
: Is that really the issue here?
: I’m sure there’s a deck around here somewhere. We just have to look around.
: Okay, so...not the King’s Game...
: With all due respect, Sana, I think we should avoid any game that could potentially give Sensei control over everyone in the room.
: Sensei can do anything he wants to me. I’m more worried about what Ami’s commands would be. Especially now that she’s already given her dare away.
: There’s...that one with the bottle?...
: Ooh, good idea! Let’s play in groups! Sensei and I will spin our own bottle on the table and the rest of you can go play in the corner.
: Aww, come on Ami! Don’t you want to kiss me again? We had so much fun the last time!
: How about “Never Have I Ever?”
: Huh...I guess that could work. I think we’d need to set some ground rules, though. I feel like that game could go sour pretty quickly if someone says the wrong thing.
: Like “Never have I ever seen my uncle’s penis?”
: Yes, Ami. Exactly like that. Good job.
: I’ll play...that game...
: May I propose that our primary rule be that no one says anything pertaining to Sensei at any point? I feel as if avoiding him entirely is the only safe option right now.
: Why would you suggest a game he can’t even participate in?
: Just look at him. I doubt he’ll be participating in anything we do.
: Heheh! He’s probably still a little exhausted from our talk.
: Don’t we need, like...drinks to play that, though? All we have is soda and I’m not about to give myself diabetes for the sake of a game.

: We can play for points instead. Whoever has done the least amount of stuff by the end of the game will be deemed the “Angel of purity.” I’ll have Geoffrey make a trophy. He has smithing skills, you know.
: So, should we have him start engraving Sana’s name on the trophy now? Or would you prefer to wait until he’s done cleaning up after a bunch of our classmates?
: Hey! I’m a good girl. I’ve got a shot at winning too. Don’t count me out just yet, jerk.
: Same here! I think we’ve all got a good shot! For all we know, Sana could be the biggest freak out of all of us.
: I guess there’s only one way to find out — so why don’t I start?
: Never have I ever...stalked someone on social media. Raise your hand if you have.
: Tch. That was a cop-out question. You barely even use social media.
: I stalked Noriko when she joined the class. I was intimidated by her love for Sensei and thought it may outweigh mine. But now I firmly believe I love him more than anyone. Even Ami.
: Wait...so...I get a point if...my hand isn’t raised...right?
: The opposite. Think of the points as demerits. You want as few as possible, and the person with the least amount whenever we stop wins.
: That sounds...a little confusing...
: It’s probably easier when there’s alcohol involved. We’ve never really done this before.
: Never have we ever done this before, you mean.
: Ooh, you should do “Never have I ever made a good joke” for your next one. That’s a sure-fire way for you to cut down the lead, Ami!
: I will end you.
: So...Maya and I...both don’t have any points?...
: I just want to make sure I’m...doing the right thing...
: That is correct. Now, seeing as I went first, it’s someone else’s turn to-
: Never have I ever...been outside of Kumon-mi!
: That is a personal attack. You know I’m not from here.
: Darn it. I’ve got two points already?! I wanted to be the angel of purity!
: Ayane? Really? You’ve left Kumon-mi before?
: Mhm! I went sledding in Aomori with my dad when I was little. But it was before I ever met you, so you can’t get mad at me for not inviting you.
: I’m not mad. I’m perfectly fine with never leaving this place.
: Then boy do I have good news for you.
: Even if we could leave, I mean.
: I’m the same way. Aomori was fun and all, but I love it here. I’m never planning on leaving.
: Well I, for one, would like to get out of here as soon as possible.
: I’ve...never left either, but...I don’t really care either way...
: Hey, why don’t you go next? You’re the only one without any points so far. Why not try and extend the lead a little bit?
: Um...uhh...okay.
: Then...um...never have I ever...k...kissed a boy...
: I’ll call Geoffrey in a few minutes and have him start on the trophy.
: Ayane I...already...uhh...but...you too, Maya?...
: Does that surprise you?
: It sure doesn’t surprise me.
: Um...who...who was-
: He goes to a different school. You don’t know him.
: Oh...uhh...oh...okay...
: So, since Sana’s already going to win, why don’t the three of us start taking bites out of each other? I think a little infighting between the original members of the Love Squad sounds kind of fun.
: So long as you promise to not get weird about it.
: I think I can do that.
: I can’t! Never have I ever touched myself in school.
: What? Your girl needs some points.
: In my defense, puberty is very hard on my body sometimes and I was simply doing what needed to be done.
: I don’t have anything to say in my defense. I was just having a weird day.
: And so the lead begins to shrink...
: Not for Sana, though. She-
: Sana?!?!
: Uhh...
: It’s...umm...I think it’s like...what Ami said...
: Well now I feel weird for not doing it! Could you guys seriously not wait until you got home? Doing that in school is-
: Oh...Wait. No.
: I think I did do it once, actually.
: Maybe?
: Did I?
: I honestly can’t remember. Can I still just...not get this point, though? I’m starting to feel impure.
: I’d like to hear what your argument against impurity would be, seeing as you just asked a room full of teenage girls about public masturbation in front of an adult male.
: Oh, right. Sensei’s here. He’s been so quiet that I kind of forgot.
: He also hasn’t raised his hand for anything so, in a roundabout way, I think he’s technically winning now that we know Sana plays with herself in school.
: That’s right...
: And everywhere else.
: Uhhhhhhh...
: Umm...Sana? You don’t have to really...share those details with us, you know. The question was just about school. You can leave it at that.
: I did it in the park last week. I think somebody saw me.
: Sana!
: I do it on the train...the bus...I even did it at your party...
: Ayane...
: What? Why are you-
: Wait...no. No no no no no.
: Now?...It’s not seriously happening now, is it?!
: What’s happening now? What are you guys talking about?
: I want to do it in here...
: I want to do it right now...
: I can feel it again...swimming through me...I need to let it out. I need to 66 65 65 6c 20 74 68 65 20 6c 69 67 68 74.
: Hah...hah...oh no...oh no...not again...
: What do we do?! What’s going on with her?!
: What’s going on with who? Seriously, what are you guys freaking out about?
: Sana, obviously! Sana! You should know by now she isn’t like this! This isn’t her!
: Sana...Sakakibara? From Ms. Watabe’s class? Are you guys friends or something?
: Ms. Watabe’s class?! She’s right here! She’s our friend! She’s-

: No. No, no, no. Bad Ayane. You’re supposed to keep calm. This is normal. This is how these things work now. Things are going to be weird and you just have to deal with it. That’s your life. Your new life.
: You can cry later.
: It came without me knowing...
: This isn’t normal at all...
: It’s going to be okay. Everything is going to be okay.
: Ayane, you’re seriously starting to scare me. If something is going on, please tell me about it. I want to be there for you.
: Sensei...
: Are you-
: Would it be...okay if I...sang a song?
: Sure, Sana! Go right ahead!
: You? Really?
: My little girl is all grown up!
: I’m...not very good, but...
: I just figured that...I should try and...put myself out there...a little more...
: Especially if...
: If I’m ever going to...
: THE WORLD IS ENDING AND WE ARE ALL GOING TO DIE!
: Wow...I had no idea Sana had such a fantastic singing voice. I wonder why she’s been keeping it a secret for so long?
: Yeah, I’m surprised as well. This is one of my favorite songs.
: How do you feel about it, Ami? You used to love this song, didn't you?
: Ami? You-
: She...
: She’s...gone?
: I didn’t even see her get up. Did she go to the bathroom or something?
: I don’t know...I didn’t see her get up either.
: She went out into the hallway.
: Oh, nice of you to join us. And why? For what? She wasn’t trying to get you to come with her again, was she?
: She said someone was calling her name.
: Who? We’re all in here. There’s no one who-
: Maya...
: What? I’m trying to figure out-
: There’s something in the hallway...
: What do you mean there’s-
: Something...in...
: That’s...
: That’s not what I think it is...is it?
: I don’t...
: It’s calling to me now too.
: You’re not going anywhere. Stay put.
: What?! And you are?! Seriously?!
: You’re more than welcome to stay here with Sensei while I check on Ami.
: Absolutely not! I can’t let you go out there alone!
: Maya, that’s blood. That’s definitely blood. I don’t like this.
: She is at that age.
: Sensei, sit down. Now.
: Oh my God. What do we do? Is this a reset? It is, right? It’s just part of the...the thing, right?!
: If it is, I can’t feel it. And I have no idea if that’s a good or a bad thing. It’s never happened before.
: If you guys find Ami, can you ask her what’s for dinner tonight? I’m starting to feel a little peckish.
: Sure, Sensei. We’ll do just that.
: Oh my God. We’re going out there? Shouldn’t we just call the cops instead? Wouldn’t that be the right thing to do if that’s really-
: Stay here if you’re just going to cry. I’ll go alone.
: I’m coming, okay?! Stop thinking you can do everything alone!
: Welp! Looks like it’s just you and me now, Sana.
: Sensei...
: Wanna put it in?
: No no no no no no no...
: No no no no no No No No No No NO NO NO NO NO NO NO NO NO NO!
: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
: AAAAHHH!!! AAAAAAHHHH!!! AAAAAAHHHHHH!!! AAAAaaaaaaAAAAAAAAAaaaahhhh!!!!! AAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
: I DON’T WANT TO DO THIS ANYMORE, MAYA!!!! I CAN’T DO THIS ANYMORE! I WANT MY OLD LIFE BACK!!!!
: I think it might be a little too late for that.
: Mmh! Mmh! Mmh!
: I can’t do this. I can’t do this. I can’t do this. I can’t do this!
: I CAN’T DO THIS I CAN’T DO THIS I CAN’T DO THIS I CAN’T DO THIS I CAN’T DO THIS  I CAN’T DO THIS  I CAN’T DO THIS  I CAN’T DO THIS  I CAN’T DO THIS  I CAN’T DO THIS I-
: BLLFCHTTHHTHHTHTFRWRBWBRBR!!!!!1111!!!1111!!!!111!!!
: I want to go home...
: Get it all out of your system?
: Our friend is dead! Look at her! Shouldn’t you have a little more to say?!
: Do you think it would be more productive for me to hack my dinner out onto the floor as well?
: Someone here needs to keep a level head and that someone is obviously going to be me as you’re too busy coughing up...whatever that is.
: Do you have a heart at all?! How can you see this and feel nothing?! Are you even human?!
: Who would do this?...Why?...How?...And how didn’t we notice?...
: The “who” and “how” don’t matter. What does matter is making sure we’re on the same page.
: Ami...Ami...
: Ayane, look at me!
: You and I are the only two people who still have our minds intact right now. And if you don’t get your shit together immediately, Sensei and I could be stuck on that roof for weeks waiting for you.
: He very likely isn’t going to snap out of his delusions until he makes it up there. And I’m another story entirely.
: She’s gonna come back, right? After this is all over?
: Yes.
: I’m sure that she’ll be back.
: Now, clean yourself up. You look disgusting.
: You’re a real fucking asshole sometimes, Maya. You know that, right?
: I’m well aware, Ayane.
: Thank you.
: Hey. I know you’re probably only 5%% sentient right now, but I’ve got some bad news. Ami won’t be making dinner tonight. And also, the world is ending. Surprise.
: Now, we need to get you back home so you’re not mindlessly wandering around and-
: Woah.
: MMFGH! MMFHG! MMMNNGHHH! MMMNGHHH!!!!!!
: Never have I ever done that before.
: Hi, Maya.
: Stop smiling. It’s somehow even weirder than...whatever the hell is happening on that table right now.
: I’m sorry. I’m just really happy to be out having fun with you. That’s all.
: Right. Well, you can be happy in your bed. We’re leaving.
: But Sana hasn’t finished her song yet.
: MMMMNNGHHHHHHH!
: Yeah, I really don’t care about that.
: Come on. I’m tired of having to chase after you when-
: Maya?
